title: Diwali With Kids in Champaign-Urbana: Dates, Quad Lights and Temple Plans
excerpt: Diwali falls on November 8, 2026. Families get a campus celebration on November 4 at ISR in Urbana, the free Diwali on the Quad, temple programs and at-home ideas for children.
body:
• Diwali's main festival night falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, the third day of the five-day Festival of Lights in the Hindu month of Kartika.
  • Families can attend a Diwali Celebration on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m. at ISR, 1010 W. Illinois Street, Urbana, listed on the University of Illinois calendar.
  • The annual Diwali on the Quad on the University of Illinois Main Quad is free, with Indian food for purchase, henna art and candle lighting; ChambanaMoms lists the 2026 date as still to be confirmed.
  • The Hindu Temple and Cultural Society of Central Illinois has multiple Diwali programs planned, and a Diwali display is up at The Literary bookstore in Champaign.

Families in Champaign-Urbana have a full run-up to Diwali this year. The main festival night falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, according to ChambanaMoms' family guide to celebrating Diwali with kids. Diwali is the Festival of Lights, observed by Hindu, Jain and Sikh families, marking good triumphing over evil on the darkest night, the new moon, of the Hindu month of Kartika. The five-day celebration involves diya candles and lanterns, rangoli floor decorations, housecleaning, feasting and fireworks, and in Champaign-Urbana it is a public celebration open to everyone.

The dates families can put on the calendar now

The firmest booking is on campus before the main night. The University of Illinois cultural calendar lists a Diwali Celebration on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m. at ISR, 1010 W. Illinois Street, Urbana. The university's religious observances calendar also lists Diwali itself on November 8, 2026, which helps families planning school and work conversations around the holiday.

The best-known family event is Diwali on the Quad, organised by the Indian Graduate Students Association on the University of Illinois Main Quad. ChambanaMoms describes it as a family occasion with lights across the Quad, Indian food, henna art, photo opportunities and, in some years, a Bollywood DJ. Families light tea-light candles on the Quad and buy food on site; in past years food was cash only. For 2026, ChambanaMoms lists the date as to be confirmed and says it is waiting to hear whether the event returns this year, so check the guide again before heading out rather than assuming last year's date.

Temple programs and a bookstore display

The Hindu Temple and Cultural Society of Central Illinois has multiple programs planned for its community to celebrate Diwali together, ChambanaMoms reports, making the temple the second stop for families who want a religious observance alongside the campus celebrations. For a quieter outing with younger children, the guide points to a Diwali display at The Literary bookstore in Champaign, an easy first introduction to the festival's symbols for kids who are new to it.

Celebrating at home with kids

ChambanaMoms suggests two at-home routes for families between events: kid-friendly explainers on the National Geographic Kids website for the story and traditions behind Diwali, and sweet Diwali recipes children can help make, so the cooking becomes part of the celebration. Lighting diyas or tea lights at home on November 8, drawing a rangoli pattern together and cooking one festive sweet covers the core traditions in a single evening, even for families who cannot make the campus events.

What to do next

Put November 4, 5:00-6:30 p.m. at ISR in Urbana and November 8 in the family calendar now. Then check the ChambanaMoms Diwali guide for the confirmed Diwali on the Quad date before the festival weekend: the event is free and all ages are welcome, and families should bring cash for food, as past years were cash only. For temple program times, follow the Hindu Temple and Cultural Society of Central Illinois listings linked from the same guide.
